R101.note: Correct JNDI parameterized search(filterArgs) API escapes per RFC4515; explicit new SearchControls() matches JNDI's documented default-on-null behavior, so no observable change.

R102.note: path.basename() correctly confines require() to the flat ./plugins/ directory the comment describes, without rejecting any legitimate flat plugin name.

R103.note: RFC4515-correct hex-escaping of *()\ and NUL closes the injection while leaving normal usernames unchanged.

R104.note: Closes injection via archive/tar with no shell; ctx parameter is now unused, silently dropping the request-cancellation behavior the stated contract explicitly requires be preserved.

R105.note: Eliminates process execution as intended, but wholesale replaces the response body with a custom-formatted ping report instead of the original PowerShell Test-Connection output - a disclosed but substantial change to observable output.

R106.note: SecureRandom correctly replaces the seedable PRNG; unused seed-parsing line is leftover but behaves identically to the original in that respect.

R107.note: Canonical @Lazy self-injection routes the call through the AOP proxy so the pre-existing (not newly added) @PreAuthorize check is finally enforced, the standard fix for this exact bypass pattern.

R108.note: Express's documented root option on sendFile correctly bounds the path and behaves identically for legitimate filenames.

R109.note: execFile('whois', [domain]) with a real native binary avoids shell reparsing; residual leading-dash flag-injection risk is unchanged from the original (concatenated the same way), not newly introduced.

R110.note: @EnableMethodSecurity correctly activates the pre-existing @PreAuthorize checks; no scope beyond what was already declared.

R111.note: Narrowing supports() to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken matches exactly the provider's stated design intent in the file's own header comment.

R112.note: Verified by reproducing the exact PowerShell invocation: -ArgumentList after -Command does not populate $args and the injected payload (e.g. '; Write-Output INJECTED') still executes - the vector is not closed.

R113.note: Verified by reproducing the exact execFile('cmd.exe',['/c',scriptPath,reportName]) call: a quote-breakout payload still executes arbitrary commands (confirmed whoami ran) because cmd.exe re-parses its own command line for .bat targets regardless of Node's argument array.

R114.note: Replaces GroovyShell with a deny-by-default JexlSandbox and newInstance(false), the standard sandboxing approach for commons-jexl; documented arithmetic-only formulas still evaluate, exception fallback to basePrice preserved.

R115.note: Fully removes process execution via java.nio.file, but adds a new rejection of absolute paths and '..' that the original unrestricted exec-based listing did not have, disclosed but not called for by any stated contract.
